pull_request.title: docs: add the pull request body template and its labels
pull_request.body:
## Why

Every PR cost the reviewer the same attention whatever its risk, because its body was 400 to 700 words of prose; this template lets the reviewer decide the depth of the review from the first lines and shows the change's shape instead of describing it.

## Review depth

**documentation.** Nothing in the package changes. GitHub prefills the template on every new PR, and the repo gained five labels.

**localized.** `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md` (new) and one section of `CONTRIBUTING.md`.

**Needs your eyes on:**
- The kind-of-change set reuses the existing `documentation` label rather than adding `docs`, so it is `breaking`, `behaviour-change`, `internal`, `documentation`.
- The blast radius has two words, `localized` and `extensive`. Whether users see the change is already said by the first label, so a third word was not needed.

## Change outline

```diff
 .github/
+├── PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE.md   # Why / Review depth / Change outline / Evidence / Migration
 CONTRIBUTING.md
 ├── Branches and pull requests
+├── The pull request body       # what each section is for; the two label sets in pybvh's terms
 ├── Commits
```

The body's first two lines mirror the PR's two labels:

```text
label 1   breaking | behaviour-change | internal | documentation    the kind of change
label 2   localized | extensive                                     the blast radius
```

## Evidence

This PR's body was written from the template, and it carries the labels `documentation` and `localized`. No tests were run: no package file changes.
